plan.title: Liver QuantSeq 3' treated vs control DE
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single raw integer gene-level count matrix (12,000 genes x 6 samples, /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column) from STAR/featureCounts, with a 6-row metadata table carrying one condition column: 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples, unpaired, single batch. The research question is purely 'which genes differ between treated and control', so the plan stops at differential expression and its report — no enrichment, no pathway scope the user did not ask for.

The library is Lexogen QuantSeq FWD 3' tag-seq: one read per transcript molecule at the 3' end, with no dependence on transcript length. Two consequences drive the design. First, no length correction, no length offset, no TPM/FPKM anywhere in the plan; the raw featureCounts integers go straight into the count model (tximport is not used — these are already gene counts). Second, long genes collect fewer reads than in a full-length library at the same depth, so the pre-filter floor is lowered from the usual 10 to 5 counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size), keeping the pre-filter minimal and letting DESeq2's independent filtering do the rest.

T1S1 runs sample-structure QC before any model: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap, and library sizes, all coloured by condition. It also records what can and cannot be checked about strandedness — the protocol is declared (QuantSeq FWD is forward-stranded) but no FASTQ, BAM, or quantifier log is in the inputs, so the check is a declaration on the count matrix and the step must say so rather than imply verification. With n=6 the QC is descriptive: it can flag a sample that sits apart from its group, but it cannot establish that the groups separate.

T1S2 fits the model and tests. Median-of-ratios size factors are estimated inside DESeq2 (counts are never pre-scaled), the condition factor gets control set explicitly as the reference level so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated, the Wald test runs on ~condition, apeglm shrinks the reported fold change, and BH with independent filtering at alpha 0.05 selects the results. The GC-content bias diagnostic that the aligner-plus-counter path calls for is included but is conditional on a GC annotation being resolvable in the environment; the gene-length half of that diagnostic is dropped because a 3' library carries no length dependence. cqn and EDASeq are not installed, so a detected GC trend is reported as a caveat, not corrected.

T1S3 is the robustness second method: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test with TMM on the same filtered counts and the same design. The intersection of the two significant sets is the high-confidence result; method-unique genes are reported as a secondary set labelled by method. The union is never presented as the result.

T1S4 assembles the report: MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, the gene table carrying unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE, genes ranked by the shrunken value, the count of genes with NA p-values split by cause (Cook's outlier flag versus independent filtering), and an explicit power statement. Three per group is low power — benchmarks show count models recover only a minority of true DE genes at n=3, mostly those with large fold changes — so absence from the significant list is not evidence of no change, and the alpha stays at 0.05 rather than being loosened to compensate.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes
Low count filter for 3' tag library: at least 5 counts in at least 3 samples
Median-of-ratios size factors inside DESeq2, with GC-content bias diagnostic
~ condition with explicit reference level control, raw integer counts, no length correction (3' tag library)
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, p-value histogram inspected
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as robustness second method
Differential expression report with MA plot, dispersion plot, shrunken and unshrunken LFC, method overlap, power statement, session info

grounding.reason: edgeR quasi-likelihood is the permitted alternative and the designated second method at 2-11 replicates per group (R-0001@9a17); R-0042@54e1 requires the overlap of the two methods be reported with the intersection as the high-confidence set. Knowledge check warned that test=QLF departs from the Wald default — accepted deliberately, since this step exists to be the second method while T1S2 remains the primary Wald test.

steps.name: Differential expression report
steps.question: What is the reportable answer to 'which genes differ between treated and control', with the fit diagnostics, the effect sizes, and the power limits of a 3-vs-3 QuantSeq design stated?
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S2 and T1S3. Include, before the gene tables: the MA plot (shrunken log2 fold change against mean normalized count with significant genes marked), the dispersion plot (per-gene estimates, fitted trend, shrunken values), and the p-value histogram. Then the gene table, ranked by the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change, carrying unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE side by side, with the shrinkage estimator named in the header. State the method, the design formula ~condition, the contrast (condition, treated, control), the thresholds (padj < 0.05, BH, independent filtering on), the number of genes tested after the >=5-in->=3 filter out of 12,000, and the number of differentially expressed genes. Report the DESeq2 / edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set. Include a power statement placed before the gene tables: 3 replicates per group is low power, benchmarks show count models detect only a minority of true differentially expressed genes at this size and predominantly those with fold changes above two, so absence from the list is not evidence of no change, and adding replicates raises power more than sequencing deeper does. Record the library type (Lexogen QuantSeq FWD 3' tag-seq) and note that length-normalized units such as TPM and FPKM do not apply to it. Attach the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, all package versions, any random seed used, and the annotation source used for gene symbols if any was consulted.
steps.context: Final deliverable for the question 'which genes differ between treated and control' on 3-vs-3 human liver QuantSeq 3' tag-seq data. No enrichment or pathway analysis is in scope — the user asked only for the gene-level difference.
acceptance_criteria: MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histogram are all present and appear before the gene tables, each with a one-line statement of what it shows
The gene table is ranked by the shrunken log2 fold change and carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE in separate named columns, with apeglm named as the estimator
The report states: method, package versions, design formula, contrast direction, padj threshold and adjustment, number of genes tested after filtering, and number of DE genes
The DESeq2 / edgeR intersection is reported as the high-confidence set, with the per-method counts beside it
A power statement for 3 replicates per group appears before the gene tables
The library type is recorded as QuantSeq FWD 3' tag-seq with an explicit note that TPM/FPKM do not apply, and the strandedness status from T1S1 is carried through
sessionInfo and package versions are stored with the results, not in a separate note
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; never rank by the unshrunken estimate alone
Keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit — shrinkage does not change the test
Report the counts of NA p-values split by cause (Cook's outlier flag versus independent filtering) so the reader knows why each gene has no p-value
Do not add enrichment, gene set, or pathway analysis — the research question asks only which genes differ
State the power limit as a caution; do not adjust the significance threshold because of it
caveats: A gene not in the significant list is not shown to be unchanged at n=3
Any GC-bias trend found in T1S2 is uncorrected in this environment and must be carried into the report as a limitation on the fold-change estimates

grounding.reason: Report content follows R-0087@c53d (MA and dispersion plots), R-0085@c24d (shrunken and unshrunken LFC with lfcSE, ranked by shrunken), R-0094@6849 (power statement at 3 replicates), R-0041@059a and R-0086@becf (method, versions, thresholds, sessionInfo).
